limits: This package records static preview validation; it does not establish full UART control, H743 acceptance of valid routes/control, road acceptance, vehicle acceptance, or full-pipeline 60 FPS. Invalid test V2 frames were observed and rejected by the H743 parser in separate SWD snapshots.
The 19 runtime modules were loaded from an isolated camera filesystem; only the small performance runner was injected from RAM.

The five historical IDE rates from the pre-FIFO static preview run are complete JPEG payload read throughput. This run did not independently log per-frame decode success or dimensions. Firmware unlock clears the buffer to avoid rereading the same published buffer; the IDE run did not decode a sequence marker per frame, so independent per-frame freshness validation was not recorded.
The GUI truncates mean frame interval to integer milliseconds before computing 1000 divided by that interval; the resulting displayed FPS can be biased high and is not precise measurement evidence.
The separately decoded SDK marker rate is a host measurement and is not an IDE per-frame decode result.
The historical 60-second CDC-off headless run measured valid routes at 79.5-79.7 FPS with a no-op UART sink and no JPEG marker writes; it does not measure real UART or FIFO throughput.
The 1389-microsecond pyb.udelay experiment is a wire-time approximation, not actual UART I/O or H743 reception.
FIFO_QUEUED and QUEUED_16 indicate acceptance by the FIFO API only; neither proves UART line completion or H743 receipt. fifo_txdone is a separate completion query.
send_end_us, capture_to_send_us, send_ms, and related send timings are sampled at write API return and are not line-completion timestamps.
Firmware without WRITE_FIFO_API version 1 uses the legacy synchronous UART write path and may run below 60 FPS.

The latest IDE 65-second run measured complete terminal payload reads: six conservative rates and 3986/3986 size-matched payloads with zero read errors. This does not independently verify each JPEG decode, IDE marker freshness, or physical screen refresh.
The independent SDK marker result is a separate host decode measurement and must not be presented as IDE per-frame decode evidence.

The latest invalid-only wrapper run computed valid camera routes (607, 608, 607, 608, 606, 608 across six windows), but its sink transmitted only the fixed invalid frame, so wire_valid=0. This does not establish H743 control acceptance, road/vehicle acceptance, or full-scenario 60 FPS.

A separate 65-second CDC-closed headless run completed six windows at 79.2-79.4 FPS with valid route computation, captures, and per-window accepted counts [794, 794, 792, 794, 792, 793]. The FIFO carried 5156 fixed 16-byte V2 invalid vision frames (seq=0, valid=0, route/control fields zero) with zero busy/partial/errors and true fifo_txdone samples before/after. synthetic_RESET_KEEP was a reverse-direction OpenMV input substitute, not UART TX. SWD snapshots recorded 79 invalid observations/79 sequence rejects in 1 second and, in the earlier wrapper run, 60/60. This confirms invalid-frame receive/rejection only; valid-route acceptance/control, road/vehicle, and all-scene acceptance remain unverified. The USB CDC session was closed, but the cable remained connected. The historical 79.5-79.7 FPS headless result used a no-op sink and remains a separate non-FIFO result.
